about.title: About Compression Ratio Calculator
about.description: The Compression Ratio Calculator determines your engine's compression ratio for horsepower and performance analysis. This professional tool calculates compression ratios from cylinder volume, combustion chamber volume, and piston displacement. Essential for engine building, performance tuning, and determining fuel octane requirements. Understanding compression ratio helps optimize engine performance, determine fuel requirements, and ensure proper engine operation across different applications from street driving to racing.

faq.q: What's the ideal compression ratio for pump gas engines?
faq.a: For 91-93 octane pump gas, compression ratios of 9.5:1 to 10.5:1 are typically safe for most engines. Higher compression ratios may require race fuel or careful tuning to avoid detonation. Our compression ratio calculator helps determine the optimal ratio for your fuel type.

faq.q: How does compression ratio affect horsepower and performance?
faq.a: Higher compression ratios generally increase horsepower and thermal efficiency by extracting more energy from the air-fuel mixture. Each point of compression ratio can add 3-4% more power. However, higher ratios also increase combustion pressure and temperature, requiring higher octane fuel.

faq.q: Can I calculate compression ratio without removing the cylinder head?
faq.a: Yes, if you have the engine specifications. Use manufacturer data for bore, stroke, and combustion chamber volume. You can also measure combustion chamber volume with a burette through the spark plug hole using our compression ratio calculator.

faq.q: What happens if my engine's compression ratio is too high?
faq.a: Excessive compression can cause detonation (engine knock), which damages pistons, rings, and bearings. Solutions include using higher octane fuel, reducing compression through cylinder head work, or using thicker head gaskets to lower the compression ratio.

faq.q: How do I calculate compression ratio from engine specifications?
faq.a: Compression ratio = (Swept Volume + Combustion Chamber Volume) ÷ Combustion Chamber Volume. Swept volume = π × (bore/2)² × stroke. Our calculator automates this process using bore, stroke, and chamber volume inputs.

faq.q: What compression ratio is best for racing applications?
faq.a: Racing engines often run 12:1 to 15:1 compression ratios with race fuel (100+ octane). The optimal ratio depends on fuel octane, engine design, and intended use. Always match compression ratio to available fuel octane rating.
